title: We call Indra for you, above all peoples

words.gram: pron. adj. with the suffix -tas (ablative sense)

words.role: with viśvataḥ pari or with vaḥ
words.context: Bhāskara gives both: «जनेभ्यः पुत्रादिभ्यः» and «विश्वतो जनेभ्य उपरिस्थितम्»

sandhi.rule: visarga before pari becomes s (P. 8.3.51 (पञ्चम्याः परावध्यर्थे)), as Bhāskara notes

morphology.note: √hve ‘call’ with samprasāraṇa and the thematic vowel: hava-.

translation.literal: Indra, for you, above all peoples, we call; may he be ours alone.
translation.readable: We call Indra for you, above every people: may he be ours, and ours alone.

meaning: A short gāyatrī verse calling on Indra: the priests invoke him on behalf of the sacrificers, ‘above all peoples’, and ask that he be theirs alone — that his help go to them and not to others. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (1.6.12) it is the puronuvākyā of an offering of rice to Indra by one who wants cattle, as Bhāskara’s viniyoga states; it is also Ṛgveda 1.7.10. The use of the verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition, not to the Veda: in its source it serves another rite (see the commentary).
in_the_rite: The third mantra of Śukra’s step in the Navagraha sūktam, addressed to Indra. S names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together in the salutation that follows, without saying which mantra is whose.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara gives the setting: «ऐन्द्रं चरुं निर्वपेत्पशुकामः» — the verse is its puronuvākyā («इन्द्रं व इति गायत्री»).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara: «इन्द्रं विश्वतस्परि विश्वस्माद् उपरि हवामहे आह्वयामः»; the wish is that he be «केवलो ऽसाधारणो ऽस्तु साधको नान्येषामिति».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa on RV 1.7.10 asks the same of Indra: «इतरेभ्योऽप्यधिकमनु ग्रहमस्मासु करोत्वित्यर्थः».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Metre gāyatrī. The Ṛgveda (1.7.10) has the same words.
